the development of a theoretical model to predict the effects of radiation-induced charge deposition in dielectric materials.
the development of a theoretical model for the charge buildup and the resulting space-charge field produced in a dielectric by the photo-Comption current.
the development and testing of a new theory of radiation-induced charge buildup in dielectric materials near interfaces, including space-charge and conduction current effects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transient conductivity of the dielectrics is a major effect in determining the space-charge fields in x-ray irradiated dielectrics.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for the lower energy x-rays the transient conduction currents are the dominant effect in determining the charge deposition and space-charge fields, whereas for the higher energy x-rays, the photo-Comptons are dominant.

the transient dielectric conduction currents are the primary source of the space-charge field near the interface, and the transient conductivity gradient in the dielectric is the primary source of charge perturbation in the dielectric.
the transient conductivity gradient in the dielectric near an interface is a significant factor in the space-charge field, and hence in the perturbation of the depth-dose distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
one cannot predict the charge buildup and associated space-charge fields by assuming that the conductivity of a dielectric near an interface is the bulk radiation-induced conduction.
one must be careful to consider the conductivity gradient when modeling space-charge field buildup in dielectrics exposed to x-rays.
the conductivity gradient at an interface can be a very significant factor in the space-charge field buildup and the perturbation of depth-dose profiles.
